title: regression-bisect-playbook-run-notes-2026-11-29
content:
Context:
We observed a throughput/latency regression in the mixed-user workload that started appearing around 2026-11-20 after a cascade of small runtime changes. This doc captures the bisect run we executed on 2026-11-29, the experimental checklist (playbook-style), what we observed, and next steps.

Goal:
- Narrow commit range that introduced the 10-15% increase in p95 tail latency for mixed-sequence traffic while median latency was minimally impacted.
- Produce a repeatable test that can be run by SRE/bench owners as part of triage.

Attendees:
- Ayesha Khan (owner)
- Daniel Park (bench infra)
- Priya Raman (serving runtime)
- Omar Li (SRE)
- Sofia Anders (observability)

High-level summary of findings:
- Regression reproducible locally on the shadow cluster using the mixed-workload harness (see harness details below).
- Git bisect narrowed the suspect window to three commits touching kernel selection + batching heuristics (commits a1b2c3..d4e5f6).
- Short-term mitigation: revert batching tweak in canary (PR 6123) reduced p95 by ~9% under target traffic.
- Root cause hypothesis: slight change to "prefer-sparse-kernel" path combined with a heuristic change in batch assembly increased inter-request serialization at small qps bursts; effect amplified by cold KV cache entries in ensemble cases.

Test harness (exact config we used):
- harness repo: github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness commit: 9f8c1e3
- serving runtime image: ghcr.io/redwood/serving-runtime:nightly-2026-11-28 (includes suspect commits)
- infra: 4x A100-80GB, 32 vCPU, 256GB RAM, NVMe local; driver CUDA 12.2, cuDNN 9.0
- workload: mixed-user (40% short-seq len 32, 60% long-seq len 512), model: open-70b-quant (kv-cache enabled), ensemble fallback enabled
- load profile: steady qps 240 for 30m with microburst pattern: 10s every 5m spike to 450 qps
- bench command (representative): python run_bench.py --workload mixed --qps 240 --spike 450 --duration 1800 --model open-70b-quant --warmup 300
- tracing: p99 span capture enabled, extra logs for kernel-selection path

Baseline vs suspect snapshot (representative numbers from the run):
- Baseline (image nightly-2026-11-18): median 22ms, p95 185ms, p99 420ms, throughput stable at 240 qps
- Suspect (image nightly-2026-11-28): median 26ms, p95 205ms, p99 520ms, throughput wobble during microbursts (5-8% request drop/requeue)
- Canary after revert (PR 6123): median 23ms, p95 189ms, p99 440ms
Note: numbers averaged across three runs with identical seed; variance ~3-6% across runs.

Bisect notes (what we tested):
1) Start range: commits from 2026-11-15..2026-11-28 (40 commits).
2) Automated script performed ~log2(40) ≈ 6 bisect steps.
3) Two bisect midpoints reproduced regression; one midpoint did not—helped narrow to three consecutive commits that touch: kernel selection weight, batcher token accounting, and kv-cache priming logic.
4) Manual micro-experiments showed that toggling the kernel-selection config off (force previous kernel) returns tail latency close to baseline.

Detailed observations (evidence):
- Flame graphs on suspect build show increased time spent in "batch_assembly.wait_for_slot" during microburst spikes.
- Traces correlate increased "kv_cache.fill_miss" events with requests that see the highest latencies. The new batch accounting incremented the batch fullness threshold earlier, which caused slightly smaller batches and higher inter-request contention for gpu kernels in between batch windows.
- Ensemble fallback requests (where second-pass reranks happen) suffer more because they touch the KV cache less predictably.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Primary: batching heuristic change reduced average batch size during spikes (esp. for mixed-seq) causing elevated p95. (high confidence)
2) Secondary: kernel selection change caused a path that adds a small atomic step per request (CPU contention) which becomes visible during microbursts. (medium confidence)
3) Tertiary: KV cache eviction timing shifted due to a change in background refresh scheduling, causing more cold hits during bursts. (low confidence)

Quick experiments run and results:
- Force previous batching policy (config: batch_policy=legacy) => p95 returns to within 2-4% of baseline (run id: r-20261129-01).
- Force previous kernel selection (env FORCE_KERNEL=v1) => p95 reduces by ~7% (r-20261129-02).
- Increase batch-assembly timeout by 20ms => median slightly higher but p95 improves modestly (r-20261129-03).
- Disable ensemble fallback (control) => p95 improves ~12% (indicates ensemble path amplifies effect).

Decision and temporary mitigation:
- Rollback the batching tweak in canary (PR 6123 reverted in canary cluster). Canary metrics show target p95 improvement; we will hold the revert until deeper root cause investigation completes.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Priya: produce minimal reproducer isolating batch-assembly wait sequence (due 2026-12-02) -> write test harness variant that pins sequence types and removes ensemble randomness. JIRA: ENG-3421.
- Daniel: add microbench that reports batch-size-distribution over time and emit a histogram metric (due 2026-12-01).
- Sofia: instrument additional CPU-side atomic contention counters + flamegraphs for next bisect iteration; attach sample traces to ENG-3421 (due 2026-12-03).
- Omar: schedule a safety-canary rollout plan and update runbook notes for abort thresholds (p95 > 200ms or error rate > 0.5%) (due 2026-12-01).
- Ayesha: coordinate experiment schedule with bench infra and post results to slack channel and confluence page (done by 2026-12-02).

Runbook additions (to be merged into Confluence):
- Add "bisect checklist" section with exact harness command, seed, and expected noise ranges.
- Include guidance for toggling batch policy and kernel selection via env vars for fast triage.
- Add a short HOWTO to capture and annotate flamegraphs for triage.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Why did the small kernel-selection change interact with batch accounting? Need to inspect the interaction surface in the scheduler codepath (Priya + Engineers on kernel selection).
- Is there a workload shape we currently do not exercise in CI that would have caught this (e.g., mixed 30/70 with ensemble)? Add to weekly shadow-run matrix.

Appendix: exact commands / links used during bisect
- bisect script (local): bench-harness/tools/bisect_regression.sh --good=2026-11-18 --bad=2026-11-28 --runs 3 --harness-config mixed
- representative run logs: s3://redwood-bench-archives/2026-11-29/regress-bisect/*
- PR that reverted batching tweak in canary: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/6123
- JIRA ENG-3421: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/ENG-3421

Notes to reviewers:
- When reproducing locally, ensure the bench-harness seed is set (see harness README). The regression is deterministic with seed but amplified by system noise; run at least 3 iterations.
- If you see differing results, attach the run id and the kernel-selection logs from /tmp/bench_logs.

End of notes.
summary: Bisect run on 2026-11-29 narrowed the latency regression to batching + kernel-selection interactions; revert in canary (PR 6123) improved p95. Follow-ups assigned to produce focused reproducer, metrics, and extra tracing.
